content:
Apple has announced plans to allow users to copy and paste content between iPhone and Windows PCs, in response to Microsoft's interoperability request in the European Union. Here are the details.

The feature may be limited to the EU region

According to a discovery by MacRumors, a new entry has been added to Apple's EU interoperability request page, indicating that the company has agreed to develop a solution allowing extensions to share and import iPhone clipboard items with paired devices (including Windows PCs).

In Microsoft's initial request received on March 25, 2026, the company stated that it is currently unable to offer a feature comparable to "Universal Clipboard," which allows users to copy and paste content between Apple devices.

Microsoft further requested that Apple provide persistent clipboard access to enable continuous syncing between iPhone and Windows PCs, listing three main use cases:

Copying text or other supported content on their iPhone and pasting it directly onto a Windows PC, and vice versa. Performing common productivity workflows without switching apps to the foreground or repeatedly initiating manual transfer operations. Treating the clipboard syncing experience as a lightweight, persistent feature rather than a manual, app-driven operation.

The company argued that "cross-device copy and paste is a fundamental productivity interaction users expect to work 'seamlessly' between their primary devices," and added that its purpose "is not to replace or replicate Apple's system experience, but to enable the baseline level of cross-device productivity users already expect when working across devices."

Apple responded on April 27, stating that after an initial assessment of Microsoft's request, it had decided to "move it to the next phase of the interoperability process."

Subsequently, on June 26, Apple confirmed it would develop a relevant solution and outlined its expected functionality.

The company also explained that Microsoft will need to rely on the AccessorySetupKit framework, which has likewise been a focal point of objection in Meta's EU interoperability request aimed at supporting AirPods-like pairing functionality between users' iPhones and iPads.

In Microsoft's case, AccessorySetupKit will be used to obtain permission to share clipboard content with paired Windows PCs, with users needing to grant consent once per device.

Apple described the project as a "significant engineering undertaking" and stated that it plans to complete development by fall 2027, after which the solution will first be released in a developer beta before its official public launch.

This timeline suggests the feature could debut alongside iOS 28, though Apple has not confirmed which software version will include it.
